turns.speaker: Caroline
turns.text: Hey Marcus, quick heads-up — I added pagination to the /users endpoint this morning. Should be live in staging.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Nice, that was overdue. Did you test it with the big dataset? I remember that query was slow.

turns.speaker: Caroline
turns.text: Yeah, I ran a load test with 10k concurrent requests. The API held up under heavy load — p99 stayed under 200ms. I was honestly surprised.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Good to hear. But hey, I noticed something weird in the query log earlier — there were some customer email addresses in there. That shouldn't be logged.

turns.speaker: Caroline
turns.text: Oh no, really? I think I accidentally logged sensitive data to the query log when I was debugging the pagination. I must have included the full row instead of just the IDs.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Yeah, that's a problem. Customer data leaked into the logs — we need to scrub those ASAP. Can you check if any of that hit production?

turns.speaker: Caroline
turns.text: I'll pull the logs and redact them right now. Also, I'll add a filter to prevent that from happening again. Sorry about that.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: No worries, just be careful. We don't want a repeat of the debug credentials incident.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Hey Caroline, did you manage to clean up those logs?

turns.speaker: Caroline
turns.text: Yes, I scrubbed all the customer emails from the query log and rotated the log files. Also added a whitelist for log fields.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Good. But I have to ask — did you ever remove those debug credentials from production? I saw a suspicious login attempt this morning.

turns.speaker: Caroline
turns.text: Wait, what? I thought I removed them. I left debug credentials in production after the last hotfix — I completely forgot to disable that account.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Well, an attacker found the debug account. They tried to log in with the default password. The IDS flagged it, but we need to disable it now.

turns.speaker: Caroline
turns.text: Oh god, I'm so sorry. I'll disable it immediately and rotate all related keys. Let me check if they got any data.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: They didn't get in — the account was locked after three failed attempts. But this is a serious wake-up call. We need a better credential management process.

turns.speaker: Caroline
turns.text: Agreed. I'll write a post-mortem and propose a checklist for production deployments. And I'll double-check the pagination code too — make sure nothing else is exposed.

turns.speaker: Caroline
turns.text: Morning Marcus. I've finished the post-mortem and the new deployment checklist. Also, I re-verified the pagination — it's solid, no data leaks.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Thanks. And the debug account is fully disabled, right?

turns.speaker: Caroline
turns.text: Yes, disabled and removed from the user table. I also added a scheduled job that scans for any leftover debug accounts.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Good. Let's make sure the API holds up under heavy load again after those changes — I don't want any regressions.

turns.speaker: Caroline
turns.text: I'll run the load test again this afternoon. And I'll keep an eye on the query log to make sure no sensitive data sneaks in.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Sounds good. Let's grab a coffee after — you've earned it after this mess.

turns.speaker: Caroline
turns.text: Ha, thanks. I'll take you up on that.
